Ghent Around Ghent

Ghent 88

Gravensteen · St Bavo’s & the Altarpiece · Graslei · Patershol · SMAK

  1. Must see · Ghent

    Sint-Baafskathedraal & het Lam Gods (Van Eyck)

    Ghent's cathedral houses the world's most famous polyptych, Hubert and Jan van Eyck's 'Adoration of the Mystic Lamb' (Het Lam Gods, 1432) — still on view in situ, with a state-of-the-art visitor centre. The lower church and crypt add centuries of art.

    Look for Home of the Ghent Altarpiece

    Sint-Baafsplein, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Stad Gent (stadsbestuur, officieel), Toerisme Vlaanderen / VisitFlanders, Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  2. Must see · Chocolate, Waffles & Sweets · Ghent

    Cuberdon- & neuzekeskramen (Groentenmarkt)

    Two rival carts side by side on the Groentenmarkt sell Ghent's raspberry cone-sweets, the cuberdon or 'neuzeke' — a decades-long feud (the viral 'war of the noses') that has become city folklore.

    Groentenmarkt 1, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by VRT NWS (Vlaamse openbare omroep), National Geographic Nederland, Atlas Obscura

  3. Must see · Ghent

    Gravensteen (Kasteel van de Graven van Vlaanderen)

    The moated 12th-century castle of the Counts of Flanders in the very heart of the city — a rare intact medieval fortress with ramparts, towers and a torture-instrument collection, reached over its own drawbridge.

    Look for Moated 12th-c. counts' castle

    Sint-Veerleplein 11, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  4. Must see · Ghent

    Belfort van Gent (Belfry)

    The 91-metre 14th-century belfry, a UNESCO World Heritage 'Belfry of Belgium and France', crowned by a gilded dragon; the middle tower of Ghent's famous three-tower row, with a glass lift to a panoramic viewing gallery.

    Look for UNESCO belfry, gilded dragon

    Sint-Baafsplein, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by UNESCO Vlaanderen, Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  5. Must see · Ghent

    Graslei & Korenlei

    The medieval inner harbour on the Leie, lined with guild houses spanning Romanesque to Baroque; Ghent's most photographed quays and, at dusk, the city's living room for a drink by the water.

    Look for Guild-house harbour quays

    Graslei, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  6. Must see · Ghent

    Werregarenstraat (Graffitistraatje)

    A cobbled alley opened to street artists in 1995 and repainted constantly — a free, ever-changing open-air gallery a few steps from the City Hall. You never see the same walls twice.

    Look for Legal ever-changing graffiti alley

    Werregarenstraat, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Atlas Obscura

  7. Must see · Ghent

    Patershol

    A pocket of winding medieval lanes and cobbles behind the Gravensteen — once a tanners' and weavers' quarter, now Ghent's most atmospheric restaurant-and-café district.

    Look for Medieval restaurant quarter

    Patershol, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids)

  8. Must see · Ghent

    Vrijdagmarkt & standbeeld Jacob van Artevelde

    Ghent's grand civic square, site of markets, joyous entries and bloody guild battles for seven centuries; at its centre the 1863 bronze of Jacob van Artevelde pointing toward England. The 14th-century Toreken guildhouse stands on the corner.

    Look for Historic civic square

    Vrijdagmarkt, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  9. Must see · Ghent

    Sint-Niklaaskerk

    A pure example of Scheldt Gothic in blue Tournai stone, built from the 13th century by the merchants of the Graslei and dedicated to St Nicholas, patron of traders. The first of Ghent's three towers.

    Look for Scheldt-Gothic merchants' church

    Cataloniëstraat, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Sint-Niklaaskerk Gent (officieel), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  10. Must see · Ghent

    S.M.A.K. (Stedelijk Museum voor Actuele Kunst)

    Ghent's museum of contemporary art, built by Jan Hoet into an international name — post-war and living artists from Bacon and Broodthaers to Panamarenko, with restlessly changing shows.

    Look for Contemporary-art landmark

    Jan Hoetplein 1, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by S.M.A.K. (officieel), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  11. Must see · Ghent

    MSK Gent (Museum voor Schone Kunsten)

    The Fine Arts Museum in Citadelpark: six centuries from Hieronymus Bosch and the Flemish Primitives to Ensor and the Symbolists, in a serene neoclassical building.

    Look for Old masters to Ensor

    Fernand Scribedreef 1, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  12. Must see · Ghent

    STAM (Stadsmuseum Gent)

    The city museum set in the medieval Bijloke abbey and hospital, telling Ghent's story from Roman settlement to today — including a walk-on aerial photo of the whole city.

    Look for The story of Ghent

    Godshuizenlaan 2, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by STAM Stadsmuseum Gent (officieel), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  13. Must see · Ghent

    Sint-Michielsbrug & Sint-Michielshelling

    The stone bridge that frames Ghent's picture-postcard view — Graslei, Korenlei and the three towers all in one sweep. The single best free vantage point in the city.

    Look for The three-tower viewpoint

    Sint-Michielshelling, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  14. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Ghent

    De Dulle Griet

    Ghent's most famous beer café, with the city's largest Belgian-beer list (500+). Order the 1.2-litre house boot and you hand over a shoe as deposit, hoisted to the ceiling in a basket until you return the glass.

    Vrijdagmarkt 50, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Lost Beers (bierjournalistiek)

  15. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Ghent

    Het Waterhuis aan de Bierkant

    A canalside brown pub in a former riverside house with a waterfront terrace and around 175 beers, including its own Klokke Roeland. The classic Ghent beer stop, next to its jenever annex.

    Groentenmarkt 9, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), TOERISMELEIE

  16. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Ghent

    't Dreupelkot

    A tiny jenever house on the water beside the Waterhuis, pouring only genever — over 200 kinds, from cactus to vanilla to chocolate — served ice-cold and brimful.

    Groentenmarkt 12, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by time to momo (reisgids), Reizen & Reistips

  17. Must see · Beer & Breweries · Ghent

    Gentse Gruut Stadsbrouwerij

    Annick De Splenter's city brewery revives 'gruut' — a medieval herb blend used instead of hops — in five house beers plus a rotating 'Maîtresse'. Tours and a canalside brewery bar in the centre.

    Rembert Dodoensdreef 1, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gentse Stadsbrouwerij Gruut (officieel), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  18. Must see · Belgian & Flemish · Ghent

    Brasserie 't Klokhuys

    An authentic Patershol brasserie that does the Ghent classics properly — creamy waterzooi of farm chicken and beef stoverij braised in beer — in a warm, cosy room.

    Corduwaniersstraat 65, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), time to momo (reisgids)

  19. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ghent

    Vrijmoed

    Chef Michaël Vrijmoed's two-Michelin-star restaurant, Ghent's culinary summit — precise, produce-driven tasting menus with a celebrated cellar.

    Vlaanderenstraat 22, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide Michelin België, Vrijmoed (officieel)

  20. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ghent

    Publiek

    Chef Olly Ceulenaere's one-star restaurant, quietly one of Belgium's most influential kitchens — a set surprise menu built around vegetables, ferments and Flemish produce.

    Ham 39, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide Michelin België, Gault&Millau België

  21. Must see · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ghent

    OAK

    Chef Marcelo Ballardin's one-star OAK — contemporary, personal cooking with surprising combinations, on a quiet street near the Gravensteen.

    Burgstraat 16, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide Michelin België, Gault&Millau België

  22. Must see · Vegetarian & Vegan · Ghent

    Greenway

    Ghent's pioneering veg restaurant, open since 1996 and now fully vegan — burgers, bowls and daily specials that helped make the city Europe's self-styled veggie capital.

    Nederkouter 42, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Greenway (officieel), time to momo (reisgids)

  23. Must see · Chocolate, Waffles & Sweets · Ghent

    Tierenteyn-Verlent

    A mustard shop unchanged since the 19th century, making Ghent's pungent mustard on the premises and scooping it, still fizzing, from a cellar barrel into stoneware pots before your eyes. Founded 1790.

    Groentenmarkt 3, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Streekproduct.be (VLAM, erkende streekproducten), Culinaire Ambiance

  24. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Stadhuis Gent (Pacificatiezaal)

    Ghent's City Hall wears two faces on one block: flamboyant Late Gothic and sober Renaissance. Inside, the Pacificatiezaal recalls the 1576 Pacification of Ghent.

    Look for Gothic-and-Renaissance city hall

    Botermarkt 1, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  25. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Groot Vleeshuis

    A 15th-century covered meat market with a soaring timber roof, once where all the city's meat was inspected; now a showcase and tasting hall for East-Flemish regional products.

    Look for 15th-c. covered meat hall

    Groentenmarkt 7, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  26. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Het Groot Kanon (Dulle Griet)

    A 12,500-kg wrought-iron bombard of the 15th century, five metres long — one of the largest siege guns of the Middle Ages, nicknamed the 'Mad Meg'. It stands on the square that bears its name.

    Look for Giant medieval bombard

    Grootkanonplein, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (NL/EN), Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids)

  27. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Design Museum Gent

    An international design collection from Art Nouveau and Art Deco to contemporary, spanning an 18th-century mansion and a bold new wing.

    Look for Art Nouveau to now

    Jan Breydelstraat 5, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (NL/EN), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  28. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Boekentoren (Book Tower)

    Henry van de Velde's modernist library tower for Ghent University (1930s–40s), a listed monument of stripped concrete recently restored, with a belvedere over the city.

    Look for Van de Velde's library tower

    Rozier 9, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Boekentoren UGent (officieel), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  29. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Klein Begijnhof Onze-Lieve-Vrouw ter Hoyen

    A walled 13th-century beguinage of whitewashed houses, church and garden around a green — founded c.1234 by Joanna of Constantinople and inscribed on UNESCO's World Heritage List of Flemish Beguinages.

    Look for UNESCO beguinage

    Lange Violettenstraat 77, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by UNESCO Vlaanderen, Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  30. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Huis van Alijn

    A museum of everyday 20th-century life set in Ghent's last surviving almshouse — reconstructed interiors, home movies and objects of ordinary Flemish lives, around a quiet courtyard.

    Look for Museum of daily life

    Kraanlei 65, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  31. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Sint-Pietersabdij & Kunsthal

    A Benedictine abbey founded in the 7th century by St Amandus, with a Baroque church, a vineyard garden and ruins, now the Kunsthal Sint-Pietersabdij exhibition space.

    Look for 7th-c. abbey & garden

    Sint-Pietersplein 9, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  32. Worth the detour · Ghent

    De Vooruit / VIERNULVIER

    The socialist cooperative's 1913 festival hall, an eclectic Art Nouveau/Art Deco monument by Ferdinand Dierkens — reopened in 2026 after a major restoration as a landmark arts centre and café.

    Look for 1913 arts-centre monument

    Sint-Pietersnieuwstraat 23, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Historiek.net, Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  33. Worth the detour · Ghent

    De Krook

    Ghent's award-winning riverside library and knowledge centre (2017), a striking angular building where the Schelde meets the city — free to enter, with terraces over the water.

    Look for Riverside library landmark

    Miriam Makebaplein 1, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (NL/EN), Stad Gent (stadsbestuur, officieel)

  34. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Kraanlei (barokgevels)

    A quay of richly carved Baroque façades facing the water — 'De Fluitspeler'/'Het Vliegend Hert' (1669) and the 'House of the Seven Works of Mercy' among the finest reliefs in the city.

    Look for Carved Baroque façades

    Kraanlei, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (NL/EN), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  35. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Oude Vismijn (Sint-Veerleplein)

    The old fish market at the confluence of Leie and Lieve, its gate crowned by a Baroque Neptune; fish was sold here from the Middle Ages to the 1960s, now a brasserie and event venue facing the Gravensteen.

    Look for Baroque fish-market gate

    Sint-Veerleplein 5, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (NL/EN), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  36. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Museum Dr. Guislain

    Set in Belgium's first purpose-built psychiatric hospital (1850s), a museum on the history of psychiatry and the shifting line between 'mad' and 'normal', with a notable outsider-art collection.

    Look for History-of-psychiatry museum

    Jozef Guislainstraat 43, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), De Gentse Musea (stadsmusea-portaal)

  37. Worth the detour · Ghent

    Industriemuseum

    Machines, people and the textile boom that made Ghent the 'Manchester of the continent', in a canalside former cotton mill — working looms and the story of industrial labour.

    Look for Ghent's textile-industry museum

    Minnemeers 10, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Industriemuseum Gent (officieel), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  38. Worth the detour · Beer & Breweries · Ghent

    De Hopduvel

    A vast beer specialty shop and bar that commissions its own Gentse Tripel, alongside a huge range of Belgian and international beers, wines and spirits — the go-to for beer to take home.

    Dok-Noord 7, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by De Hopduvel (officieel), time to momo (reisgids)

  39. Worth the detour · Beer & Breweries · Ghent

    De Trollekelder

    A characterful troll-themed beer café by Sint-Jacobs with a deep, well-kept list of trappist and abbey beers and a quiet upstairs — a beer-lover's classic away from the tourist crush.

    Bij Sint-Jacobs 17, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Lost Beers (bierjournalistiek), Verloren Bieren / Het Gentsche Kroegenboek

  40. Worth the detour · Beer & Breweries · Ghent

    Het Spijker

    A historic pub in a former granary right in the centre, with two terraces — one on the bustling street, one over the Leie — and a solid local beer list.

    Pensmarkt 3, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Reizen & Reistips

  41. Worth the detour · Beer & Breweries · Ghent

    't Galgenhuisje

    By far the smallest café in Ghent, an 18th-century brown pub on the Groentenmarkt pouring its own Galgenbier — squeeze in upstairs or take a stool on the market.

    Groentenmarkt 5, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids)

  42. Worth the detour · Belgian & Flemish · Ghent

    Brasserie 't Vosken

    A typical Ghent brasserie in a striking black-and-white room directly below St Bavo's, with a big summer terrace on the square — the reliable address for stoverij and waterzooi in the centre.

    Sint-Baafsplein 19, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids)

  43. Worth the detour · French & Brasserie · Ghent

    Brasserie Pakhuis

    A grand belle-époque brasserie in a converted warehouse down an atmospheric alley — oysters, seafood and French-Italian classics under a soaring iron-and-glass roof.

    Schuurkenstraat 4, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Gault&Millau België

  44. Worth the detour · Belgian & Flemish · Ghent

    Balls & Glory

    An open-kitchen canteen serving one thing brilliantly: handmade meatballs with a molten filling, from honestly sourced meat, with mash and greens. Walk-in, no reservations.

    Jakobijnenstraat 6, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Feeling (Roularta magazine)

  45. Worth the detour · Belgian & Flemish · Ghent

    Bord'Eau (Oude Vismijn)

    A brasserie set in the Baroque old fish market at the foot of the Gravensteen, with a waterside terrace where the Leie and Lieve meet — classic dishes in one of Ghent's most scenic rooms.

    Sint-Veerleplein 5, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&Millau België, Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  46. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ghent

    Karel de Stoute

    A refined modern-French, farm-to-table table in Patershol, selected by the Michelin Guide — a small, chef-led room with a strong seasonal menu.

    Vrouwebroersstraat 2, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide Michelin België, Gault&Millau België

  47. Worth the detour · Michelin & Fine Dining · Ghent

    Roots

    A Michelin-listed Patershol restaurant serving modern, creative Belgian cooking in a relaxed room — 3–4-course lunches, longer tasting menus at night.

    Vrouwebroersstraat 5, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Le Guide Michelin België, Feeling (Roularta magazine)

  48. Worth the detour · Belgian & Flemish · Ghent

    Elders

    Chef Tom Pauweleyn's warm neighbourhood gastro-bistro, named Gault&Millau's Gastro-Bistro of the Year 2025 — creative, generous cooking off a lively square.

    Edmond Van Beverenplein 16, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&Millau België, Le Guide Michelin België

    Le Botaniste

    An organic plant-based canteen — buddha bowls, whole-food sushi, tonic wines — small, warm and central; the Ghent original of a concept now exported worldwide.

    Hoornstraat 13, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Be Vegan (België), time to momo (reisgids)

  50. Worth the detour · Vegetarian & Vegan · Ghent

    Lokaal

    A daylight bistro named for its ecological, local-produce philosophy — seasonal, largely vegetable-forward plates by the Glazen Straatje.

  51. Worth the detour · Vegetarian & Vegan · Ghent

    Avalon

    A long-running vegetarian restaurant in a stepped-gable house opposite the Gravensteen, with a garden terrace — organic, seasonal lunches, a Ghent veggie fixture.

    Recommended by Be Vegan (België), time to momo (reisgids)

  52. Worth the detour · Chocolate, Waffles & Sweets · Ghent

    Julie's House

    A tiny, much-loved patisserie and breakfast spot on the Kraanlei overlooking the water — cheesecakes, pies and homemade granola in a doll's-house room.

    Kraanlei 13, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Julie's House (officieel), Rutger Bakt (Rutger van den Broek)

  53. Worth the detour · Chocolate, Waffles & Sweets · Ghent

    Yuzu

    Nicolas Vanaise's minimalist chocolate boutique, among Belgium's most admired — pralines built on unexpected flavours like yuzu, tonka, truffle and pepper. In the Gault&Millau chocolatier guide.

    Walpoortstraat 11a, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&Millau België, Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  54. Worth the detour · Café & Brown Café · Ghent

    Mokabon

    A cosy coffee roastery in the heart of Ghent since 1937 — dark, nostalgic and beloved by locals as much as visitors for a proper espresso.

    Donkersteeg 35, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Mokabon (officieel), june. a travel magazine

  55. Worth the detour · Belgian & Flemish · Ghent

    De Superette

    Kobe Desramaults' bakery-restaurant — sourdough, wood-fired pizza and brunch from a Scandinavian oven — voted the country's best new concept when it opened and still a hotspot.

    Guldenspoorstraat 29, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Knack Weekend, Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  56. Worth the detour · Belgian & Flemish · Ghent

    De Frietketel

    A student-belt frituur repeatedly voted Ghent's best, famed for crisp fries and an unusually broad range of vegetarian and vegan snacks.

    Papegaaistraat 89, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Gentblogt (stadsarchief, stad.gent)

  57. Worth the detour · Belgian & Flemish · Ghent

    Otomat

    A hip wood-fired pizzeria between the Gravensteen and the Groentenmarkt whose dough is raised with Duvel yeast — 'otomat' with red sauce, 'notomat' white; you can even moor a boat and order to the quay. In the Gault&Millau guide.

    Kleine Vismarkt 3, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gault&Millau België, time to momo (reisgids)

  58. Worth the detour · Vegetarian & Vegan · Ghent

    Tasty World

    A small order-at-the-counter veggie eatery a few blocks from the Gravensteen — multigrain veggie burgers, sweet-potato fries and thick shakes; a long-running Ghent meat-free staple.

    Hoogpoort 1, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Greenway (officieel), Be Vegan (België)

  59. Deep cut · Ghent

    Groot Begijnhof Sint-Amandsberg

    A vast neo-Gothic beguinage village of some 80 houses and a central church, built 1873–76 when the beguines left the old city centre; UNESCO World Heritage and still remarkably intact.

    Look for UNESCO neo-Gothic beguinage

    Groot Begijnhof, 9040 Sint-Amandsberg, Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (NL/EN), UNESCO Vlaanderen

  60. Deep cut · Ghent

    Geeraard de Duivelsteen

    A 13th-century Scheldt-Gothic stone castle named for the swarthy knight Geeraard 'the Devil' — over the centuries an armoury, monastery, seminary, asylum and prison, now a striking waterside landmark.

    Look for 13th-c. 'Devil's castle'

    Geraard de Duivelstraat 1, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (NL/EN), Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids)

  61. Deep cut · Ghent

    Sint-Baafsabdij (ruïne)

    The evocative ruins of the abbey where Ghent was born — cloister, refectory and lapidary museum of stone fragments, at the old confluence of Leie and Schelde.

    Look for Ruins where Ghent began

    Gandastraat 7, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  62. Deep cut · Ghent

    Citadelpark & Plantentuin UGent

    The city's largest 19th-century park — winding paths, a grotto, bandstand and, at its edge, the university's botanical garden with tropical glasshouses. Home to MSK and S.M.A.K.

    Look for City park & botanical garden

    Citadelpark, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Wikipedia (NL/EN)

  63. Deep cut · Ghent

    Bloemenmarkt Kouter

    Ghent's daily flower market on its most elegant square, at its liveliest on Sunday mornings when a brass kiosk plays and locals take an oyster-and-white-wine aperitif.

    Look for Daily flower market

    Kouter, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids), Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme)

  64. Deep cut · Ghent

    Portus Ganda

    Recommended by Visit Gent (officiële stadstoerisme), Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids)

  65. Deep cut · Ghent

    Rabot (Rabottorens)

    Look for 15th-c. twin-tower water gate

    Rabotplein, 9000 Gent, Belgium

    Recommended by Wikipedia (NL/EN), Gent, De Kuip (lokale erfgoedgids)

  66. Deep cut · Ghent

    De Wereld van Kina: het Huis

    A family nature-and-science museum — cabinets of animals, minerals and the human body, plus a botanical garden across town — the former Michel Thiery school museum.

53 sights and 55 places to eat across Ghent and its region — from the moated Gravensteen and St Bavo’s Cathedral with the Ghent Altarpiece (Van Eyck) to the Graslei/Korenlei quays, the Belfry, the medieval Patershol, SMAK/MSK and the Werregarenstraat graffiti alley, out to Sint-Martens-Latem and the Leie. A food canon all its own: Gentse waterzooi and stoverij, the purple cuberdon (neuzekes) carts, Tierenteyn mustard, the Gruut city brewery and the boot of beer at Dulle Griet — plus Europe’s veggie capital.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish or beer — a label alone doesn’t qualify. The Ghent canon: waterzooi, Gentse stoverij, the cuberdon (neuzekes), Tierenteyn mustard and a strong veg bench — with the Gruut brewery and jenever at ’t Dreupelkot. Beer & breweries are their own grouped layer. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it serves.

Web-searched in-language and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, Gault&Millau, De Standaard, Het Nieuwsblad, VRT NWS, Visit Gent, beer authorities and vetted local creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor/RateBeer never count toward the two-source bar.

Cleo beta — every place is carried from the current live guide, with its sources. Map tiles: © OpenStreetMap contributors; Esri. All destinations.
